filmIssues: The pull-back idea is legible, but the opening frame is awkwardly over-tight: at t=0-0.4 the young man's silhouette is clipped at the left and bottom edges and the bunting and headline bars are cropped, so the page does not open on a composed picture.

The foreground man shows a visible horizontal slice/tear at table height in the early frames, with his torso, extended arm and lower body misaligning across the table edge; the settle entrance plus strong parallax makes the cut-out read as separated from its painted-over spot.

Because the move is damped/clamped by the tight first framing, the handshake that is meant to be the reveal is not cleanly centred or readable — the hand sits at the table edge amid the slice, while the four officials remain small in the distance.
The final full-plate frame at t=1 is a good dwelling picture and the halftone-shimmer suits the 1950s lithograph style, but the faulty opening and tearing outweigh that.

rounds.verdict: Do not publish as-is: the film is coherent and era-appropriate, but its damped pull-back is too timid to earn its place over a plain zoom — it needs the bolder tight-handshake-to-full-party reveal in the revised plan.
filmIssues: The pull-back is legible but timid and generic: zoom falls only 1.24 to 1.0 with tiny pans, so across the six frames it reads as little more than a plain centred zoom in reverse, not as a purposeful widening from the singled-out handshake to the farewell party and the weight of responsibility.
Parallax is almost absent: the young man (depth 0.85) and bunting (depth 0.45) barely separate, and with near-zero drifts there is no visible foreground/background layering to justify the cut-outs.

No subject incoherence is visible — the man's arm stays joined to his torso and over the table, there is no doubled edge, halo or ghost, and no layer clips the frame edge awkwardly; the seated row and table correctly stay together in the background.

The first frame is a serviceable, slightly tight opening on the man and handshake and the last frame is a good full-plate picture to dwell on, but the intervening move is too small and even to feel good as a reveal in either direction.
Halftone-shimmer is fitting and subtle for the 1950s offset-lithograph print style and does not damage the flat inks.

rounds.verdict: A clear pull-back concept with a good final frame, but the over-tight, edge-clipped opening and the figure sliding against the table make it unpublishable as rendered.
filmIssues: The pull-back idea is legible — tight on the young man and his outstretched hand, then widening to the full farewell party — but the opening at zoom 1.38 is awkwardly cropped: the young man, table and bunting are all clipped at the left/top edges in t=0, so the page does not open on a good picture.

Because cut-1 is at depth 0.9 against the background table, the foreground figure slides noticeably against the table edge as the camera pulls back. The table line cuts across his torso/arm and his lower body reads as detached in the early frames, weakening the handshake gesture rather than clarifying it.

The move is essentially a single damped pull-back, close to a reverse push-in: no entrance, reveal or layer action makes the 'singled out' moment land. The final full-plate frame is good to dwell on and the halftone-shimmer/print texture is fitting and subtle, but the start framing and layer separation keep it below publishable.

plan.rationale: Make the intended story unmistakable: open much tighter on the young man's extended hand over the table (the moment of being singled out), then pull back decisively to the full farewell party, bunting and headline bars so the responsibility visibly widens around him.
